kind: code (tools MILESTONE, Phase 9 SERIAL — adapter/tools.ts + a two-line extension to core/gates-phase.ts). Tool: conductor_dispatch_wave — the §4.2 wave driver. It computes the wave through core/schedule nextWave, runs one async pipeline per wave member through the SHARED fan-out engine (so the orchestrator model never interleaves items by hand), and performs PLAN_REVIEWED->EXECUTING on its first call. New export: handleDispatchWave (+ DispatchWaveInput / DispatchWaveResult), following the handleX convention. Driven through the FAKE SDK + a real on-disk fixture repo.

correctionsToDraft: GAP-1 FIX, made concrete: extend the EXECUTING branch of legalTools to also set conductor_dispatch_wave legal when the wave it ALREADY computes is non-empty (wave.parallel.length > 0). Do NOT touch the `recommended` derivation — the per-item stage tool stays the recommendation, so the continuation engine's behaviour is unchanged and no committed gates-phase row changes meaning. GAP-2 FIX, sharpened to stay inside G4: the draft's 'injectable per-stage executor table' is approved as DEPENDENCY INJECTION (the same pattern as the injected Fanout, the injected clock and VerifyOptions.staleMarkerMs) — but its DEFAULT table must wire ONLY handlers that exist at HEAD, and a member that reaches a stage with no committed executor must STOP there with a disposition naming the missing stage. It must never throw 'not implemented' and never carry a placeholder executor: at 9.4c a wave genuinely cannot publish, because conductor_publish does not exist yet, and the driver should say so rather than pretend. The 9.4c tests inject RECORDING executors to pin ordering for the not-yet-built stages, and the Phase 9 milestone gate re-runs the ordering rows against the real 9.5a/9.5b handlers once they land.
reusesExisting: core/schedule.ts nextWave(queue, items, config) -> WavePlan — THE wave-membership computation (dependency-ready = deps PUBLISHED, pairwise fileScope-disjoint with degenerate-scope serialization, blocked/deferred/PUBLISHED excluded, maxImplementers cap, DAG-depth-then-id order, non-empty rationale). The driver CALLS it and re-derives none of its rules.
core/schedule.ts readFanout(stage, config) — the per-stage reader count for the batched read stages.

adapter/fanout.ts createFanout(...) -> {dispatch, dispatchWave} — the concurrency engine: per-model grouping, maxReaders admission, freeze-aware HOLD of write-capable jobs (journal fanout/subsession.hold, released via TreeState.onClear), per-job watchdog armed before create, bounded retry. §4.2: the driver SHARES this engine's budget — it must not open a second session pool or re-implement admission.
adapter/fanout.ts TreeState {isFrozen, onClear} — the P7 wiring surface bridging evidence verify markers to fanout hold/release.
core/fsm-run.ts legalRunTransition + RunTransitionContext — the P3 gate (planReviewGate: survivingMajors === 0 OR round >= max). The exit condition lives there and is never re-derived in the handler.

adapter/state.ts StateStore — handlers are the ONLY writers of run/item state (G6); assertions read persisted files through the store, never logs.
tests/fixtures/fake-sdk.ts makeFakeSdk — the ORDERED call log every interleaving/batching/serialization assertion reads.

core/journal-events.ts EVENTS — the closed vocabulary already covers everything the driver emits (fanout: subsession.dispatched/hold/complete/retry/abort; fsm: transition; state: item.updated). NO widening is needed and none is permitted.
specGaps: GAP (repeat calls vs the phase gate) — RESOLVED, see correctionsToDraft GAP-1. §3.4 says dispatch_wave advances PLAN_REVIEWED->EXECUTING 'on its first call' and §3.2 calls it the run's work engine; both imply later calls from EXECUTING for multi-wave runs. Committed legalTools offers it only at PLAN_REVIEWED. 9.4c extends the EXECUTING branch when the wave is non-empty. Raised at the Phase 9 milestone gate.
GAP (stages that do not exist yet) — RESOLVED, see correctionsToDraft GAP-2. conductor_item_review lands at 9.5a and conductor_publish at 9.5b, AFTER 9.4c in the serial order.

GAP ('item order' is never defined): §4.2 says publish runs 'serially in item order' without saying which. RESOLUTION: the deterministic §4.2 wave order — WavePlan.parallel order (DAG depth ascending, then item id ascending), the same order every other §4.2 rule and the legalTools recommendation already use.

GAP (batching rendezvous is undefined): §4.2 requires like stages to batch across members AND requires that a blocked member not stall the others, but never says how long to wait to coalesce. RESOLUTION (deterministic, no timing windows): the driver advances the wave stage-by-stage; at each READ stage it dispatches ONE fanout group holding the jobs of every member that completed the previous stage and is still active; a member that drops out (blocked, deferred, env-failed) leaves all later groups and the survivors proceed without waiting. Write stages never batch — they serialize per tree (§4.3).

GAP (summary shape): the 'compact per-item disposition summary' has no §2 schema. RESOLUTION (return value only — no persisted artifact, no SCHEMAS widening): {runState, wave: {parallel, rationale}, items: [{itemId, state, blocked | null, deferred | null, envError | null}]}. 'Compact' is pinned as: never embeds full §2.4 queue-item or §2.5 item JSON.

GAP (empty first wave): if every item is blocked at the plan-review cap the first call computes an empty wave, and the plan does not say whether the transition still happens. RESOLUTION: YES — the transition is unconditional on the first call. Otherwise conductor_report is unreachable and the run wedges at PLAN_REVIEWED, which is the same class of livelock the P3 binding exists to prevent (and the same class as C-032's deferred-dependency wedge).

assertions.text: conductor_dispatch_wave computes wave membership by CALLING core/schedule nextWave, never a re-derivation: with a fixture queue holding two ready scope-disjoint items PLUS a blocked item, a deferred item and a dependency-unready item, the driver runs pipelines for exactly WavePlan.parallel — the fake SDK's call log contains ZERO sub-sessions attributable to the excluded three, and the summary carries nextWave's rationale verbatim

the FIRST call performs PLAN_REVIEWED->EXECUTING (run.json persists EXECUTING through the store; the fsm 'transition' event is journaled through the closed vocabulary); a repeat call on an already-EXECUTING run performs NO further run transition; and an EMPTY first wave still transitions, returning a zero-member summary with nextWave's no-items rationale

MANDATORY DEFERRED BINDING (P3): the PLAN_REVIEWED->EXECUTING edge goes through core/fsm-run legalRunTransition with context derived from PERSISTED state — Run carries planReviewRounds, not survivingMajors — so iff run.planReviewRounds < config.workflow.planReviewMaxRounds the review exited clean and the handler passes survivingMajors:0, else it passes {round, max}. BOTH persisted shapes advance to EXECUTING (two cases: clean exit and cap exit); a clean plan review must never livelock entry to EXECUTING

the Gap-1 fix, asserted through the PURE gate: core/gates-phase legalTools offers conductor_dispatch_wave in EXECUTING whenever the wave is non-empty, and does NOT offer it once every item is settled — while `recommended` is UNCHANGED in both cases (still the §4.2 wave-order-first item's stage tool, or conductor_report). A second dispatch_wave call on a multi-wave run therefore passes the same legality step the first did

the driver runs TWO members' pipelines concurrently through the SHARED fan-out engine, and the fake SDK's ordered call log PROVES interleaving: at least one of item B's sub-session calls lands strictly between two of item A's — never a full serial drain of A before B begins. This is the behaviour §4.2 promises and that no orchestrator-driven design could deliver

like stages batch across members: when both members reach the vet stage, BOTH items' critics dispatch as ONE fanout group carrying readFanout('vet', config) critics per member, asserted as one contiguous dispatch group in the call log; a member that has dropped out is absent from later groups and its absence delays nothing

writes serialize per tree (the §4.2 ordering guarantee the DRIVER owns; default parallel.writes 'off' means one shared tree): the call log shows at most ONE write-capable implementer sub-session in flight in the shared tree at any moment — A's and B's implementer sessions never overlap — while read-stage sub-sessions still overlap freely. The fanout freeze-hold mechanism is REUSED, not reimplemented

publish is serial in item order: the REVIEWED->PUBLISHED stage executions run strictly one at a time in the deterministic §4.2 wave order (DAG depth then id), item B's publish never beginning before item A's completes even when B reaches REVIEWED first (the git index is a singleton). Pinned through the injected stage-executor seam because conductor_publish lands at 9.5b; re-run against the real handler at the Phase 9 gate

the G4 half of the Gap-2 resolution: with the DEFAULT executor table (only handlers committed at HEAD), a member that reaches a stage no committed handler serves STOPS there and is reported with a disposition NAMING the missing stage — the driver neither throws 'not implemented', nor silently skips the stage, nor advances the item past work that never happened

a member that BLOCKS mid-pipeline does not stall the other: the sibling's pipeline continues to its own completion (the call log shows sibling dispatches AFTER the block lands), and dispatch_wave RETURNS when the wave is drained-or-blocked — the blocked member is reported blocked in the summary, read back through the store, never awaited

the return is a compact per-item disposition summary: exactly one row per wave member carrying {itemId, final state, blocked | null, deferred | null, envError | null}, plus the run state and the wave rationale; 'compact' is ASSERTED — the return embeds no full §2.4 queue-item or §2.5 item JSON

MANDATORY DEFERRED BINDING (P7, from C-025 F2 + C-024 F6): a leaked freeze marker becomes an env-fail, never a silent wave hang. The fixture leaks a stale verify marker (dead pid, or startMs beyond staleMarkerMs) in the shared tree so the fanout engine HOLDS a write-capable member job (journal fanout/subsession.hold); when the evidence layer breaks that marker (runVerify's staleMarkerBroken path) the driver's TreeState MUST fire onClear so the held job releases and the wave completes; the broken marker surfaces as an anomaly in the journal and in the member's disposition. If no verify ever runs to break it, the driver env-fails the held job rather than hanging. The test proves wave termination WITHOUT the per-job watchdog firing
